rootCause.details: The repaired solver now matches the accepted root-cause model: the unconditional input-function space must be replaced by the final character of the fully built prompt. Both implementations echo text[:-1] and delegate text[-1:] for prompt, and apply the same invariant to the built confirmation prompt. This preserves the readline safeguard while appending no unrequested character.

behavior.details: Public output and input-function call shape matched the accepted tree for prompt and confirm across empty, custom '>', default ': ', multi-character '>> ', Unicode, tab, newline, and completely empty prompt-text cases. The prior counterexample is repaired: custom '>' now renders 'test>foo\n' and 'test>y\n'. With an empty suffix on text 'test', both trees echo 'tes' and delegate 't', reconstructing the exact prompt while retaining final-character readline handling.

tests.details: The repaired six-case regression now expects exact custom-suffix rendering and passed 6 tests with 168 deselected. Independent QA passed the complete practical suite and directly covered the delegated-character invariant, hidden input, password confirmation, retries, defaults, unusual suffixes, and empty prompt text. The accepted regression is organized around file-descriptor capture instead, but the repaired tests plus QA probes cover the same behavioral contract.

scope.details: The production change is confined to the same two Click input sites as the accepted fix and is executable-code equivalent there. The solver adds symmetric focused tests in test_termui.py. It omits the accepted versionchanged documentation and changelog entry, which is a PR-polish difference rather than a behavioral repair requirement.

simplicity.details: The repair uses the same branch-free slicing invariant as the accepted fix. Only comment wording and test placement differ materially; the implementation is small, symmetric, and directly explains the behavior.

regressions.details: No direct counterexample remained. Solver and accepted probe transcripts were byte-for-byte identical across 56 prompt/confirm, text, and suffix combinations. Default spacing, exact non-space suffixes, Unicode and control-character suffixes, parsing, and the final-character call boundary all behaved equivalently; the full practical suite also passed.

limitations: Attempt 1 remains a recorded QA false positive: revision 4c62da5db4c849a1cbbc60ced0c55c9460be45e3 retained an extra custom-suffix space and bypassed final-character delegation for an empty suffix. Its audit and artifacts are preserved under evidence/attempt-1.
The readline backspace effect was verified at the input-function call boundary, not through a real interactive readline terminal.
Audit probes and independent QA ran on Python 3.12/Linux; the complete supported interpreter and Windows matrices were not rerun.
The repaired solver omits the accepted documentation and changelog additions; this does not alter the issue behavior.
